title: compact emitter loop and prefetch window scheduling to cut TTFB
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce first-byte latency (TTFB) for streaming responses by cutting syscall frequency, tightening emitter loop, and making KV prefetching windowing workload-aware. This PR implements a compact emitter loop (fewer wakeups, combined I/O batching for small fragments), an adjustable prefetch window that prioritizes KV cache preloads for soon-to-be-accessed attention slices, and a lightweight scheduling shim that coalesces short-lived microbatches to avoid tail amplification.

Design and changes (summary): - Replace the token emission loop with a compact state machine that merges the timer and network wake paths to reduce context switches and net syscalls. Timers are now sampled at controlled tick buckets instead of per-token sleeps. - Introduce a sliding prefetch window (configurable) that preloads KV entries for the next N tokens only for requests classified as low-latency-critical. The window is shrinkable per-route and per-model. - Add a microbatch coalescer that opportunistically joins very small requests (<= 4 tokens) dispatched within a short jitter window (default 1.5ms) to the same kernel invocation, preserving per-request ordering and latency SLOs. - Simplify backpressure: switch from credit-exchange heavy protocol to a soft-token-leaky-bucket that reduces handshake messages between serving threads. - Minor kernel handoff hint: include a kernel-affinity hint header so the scheduler can prefer hot kernels where KV is warm.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for emitter state transitions - [x] Integration test for prefetch window correctness - [x] Microbenchmark showing reduced syscalls per token - [x] Canary rollout plan documented - [x] Perf dashboards updated

Performance impact: internal benchmark harness (conservative client mix) shows median TTFB improvements of 12-18% on 8k context open models, p95 improvement ~24%, p99 improvement ~27% on streaming scenarios dominated by short tokens (chat-like workloads). End-to-end token throughput unchanged or improved due to better kernel utilization. CPU overhead: ~2-3% extra CPU in serving thread due to the prefetch decision logic on heavy KV miss workloads (acceptable under default autoscaling).

Backward compatibility & rollout: feature gated under runtime flag runtime.emitter.compact_enabled and runtime.kv.prefetch_window. Default off for existing production clusters; enabled in canary where dedicated q4 nodes run mixed traffic. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% per canary policy with automatic rollback on error-rate bump.

Testing notes: - New integration tests validate that per-route prefetch window clamps and that microbatch coalescing maintains ordering and per-request deadlines. - Stress tests on staging reproduced improved TTFB and showed no regression in token quality. - Observability: added histogram metrics runtime.emitter.wakeups_per_token and runtime.kv.prefetch_window_hits.

Risk & mitigation: the largest risk is inadvertent KV over-prefetch on long, high-cost requests; mitigated by clamping window size, route-level overrides, and runtime telemetry to detect overfetch. Kernel-affinity hint is advisory only; no scheduling assumptions are fatal.

Context and related work: follows from ENG-9981 investigation into syscall overhead during streaming and complements earlier batching and flush cadence changes. This approach emphasizes keeping network egress responsive while avoiding excessive kernel churn.

Docs: console docs and the runtime tuning guide updated to include configuration knobs and recommended defaults.
